evidence.quote: Lloyds Metals & Energy has transformed from a small-cap sponge iron producer into a fully integrated mining-to-metals platform.
In FY26, it crossed ₹1,00,000 Cr market cap, ₹17,000 Cr consolidated revenue, and ₹3,900 Cr consolidated PAT.

The company operates across: Iron ore mining (21.96 MnT production, 119.6% YoY growth), Pellet manufacturing (3.03 MnT, 4 MTPA capacity, 100% utilization within 4 months), DRI/Sponge iron (ramping 360 KTPA expansion), Steel (1.2 MTPA wire rod mill commissioning in Q4FY26), Copper (DRC assets, 50% stake in CHEMAF, 12,000 TPA SX-EW plant), Mining services through Thriveni (₹8,000 Cr revenue, ranked #1 coal mine in India).
VAP share doubled from 20% to 32% of revenue and from 11% to 30% of EBIT.
LLOYDMET's iron ore reserves (55 MnT EC at Surjagarh, valid to 2057) give it a multi-decade resource advantage.
India targets 300 MTPA steel capacity by 2030 and 500 MTPA by 2047.
The ₹13,500 Cr capex has been funded with debt.
LLOYDMET's 34% EBITDA margin and 56% ROCE are best-in-class among Indian metals and mining companies.
